children: Food Empire prioritizing its profitability over sales could translate to higher margins, positioning the Singapore-listed instant coffee maker for a stronger net margin and earnings in 2H, say UOB Kay Hian analysts in a note. The analysts expect 2H earnings to rise 7% on half, citing the company's larger emphasis on margins. The company's established brands, strong market positions and broad-based presence across markets and products also underpin the resilience of its business, the analysts add. Still, UOB KH lowers its price-to-earnings multiple peg due to a broader industry derating, leading to the brokerage trimming its target price to 3.00 Singapore dollars from S$3.49. UOB KH retains its buy rating. Shares fall 1.2% to S$1.63. (megan.cheah@wsj.com)
